Putrid Warrior: Filler two-drop for WB. The 55.5% GIH WR is respectable but the drain/gain mode only matters if it connects, and a vanilla 2/2 body rarely does in a grindy format. Late-pick roster-filler that gets cut when your curve is deep.
Krosan Tusker: Solid green role-player masquerading as a fatty. The 56.5% GIH sits on the cycling mode — a fixing-plus-card that smooths any green deck, so you rarely hard-cast the 6/5. Never a dead draw; take it as a curve-topper you can also throw away. C+ undersells the flexibility.
Mass Hysteria: Trap. F grade, 7% play rate, and no meaningful WR sample — a symmetric global haste enchantment does nothing for MKM's grindy guild-midrange plans and helps your opponent as much as you. Never play it.
Spell Snare: Trap/sideboard. A narrow hard counter that only hits mana-value-2 spells — dead against most of what matters and unplayable maindeck in a grindy guild format. F grade and 9.5% play rate agree; leave it in the box.
Ghost Quarter: Trap. A colorless land whose only relevant mode blows up one of the opponent's lands while handing them a basic — a nonbet in a two-color guild format with no real nonbasics to punish. F grade and a 4.6% play rate say it: last-picky, don't run it.
Enlisted Wurm: Solid GW midrange payoff: a 5/5 for six that free-casts a smaller nonland spell off cascade, netting real tempo. The 60.6% GIH with a fat +4.9 IWD confirms it plays like a two-for-one bomb-lite whenever your curve is deep enough to hit. B+ and an early ALSA — a fine mid-pick body for Selesnya.
Kuldotha Rebirth: Filler at best. Three goblins for one mana reads well but demands a spare artifact to sacrifice, and a flat 50% GIH WR with negative IWD confirms it's a build-around that rarely pays off in a grindy midrange format. Only for a dedicated aggro/sac shell with tokens to spend, otherwise leave it.
Molten Psyche: Trap. A symmetric wheel that only pays off with a metalcraft artifact count you won't reliably hit in a guild-midrange format, and even then just pings for a few. F grade and 5% play confirm it — leave it in the pack.
Leonin Relic-Warder: Role-player artifact/enchantment hate stapled to a 2/2. The negative IWD (-2.2) exposes it: it's a 55% card because it's played in white decks, not because it wins games — the exile is temporary and often nothing to remove. Fine WW body, unexciting.
Gnaw to the Bone: Sideboard-only lifegain, and barely that. Null WR with 4.3% play rate confirms nobody runs it — the graveyard payoff is too slow for a grindy get-on-board format. D grade earned; leave it in the pack unless you're desperately racing a specific aggro matchup.
Stromkirk Captain: Tribal filler that only pays off in a Vampire-dense BR build you can't reliably assemble in this format. 49.5% GIH and +0.5 IWD say a below-water 2/2 first striker most of the time; the B- grade overrates it. Pass unless you're deep in vampires.
Burden of Guilt: Filler pseudo-removal. A repeatable tapper never kills, just locks one blocker down for {1} a turn, and the 49.4% GIH WR with negative IWD confirms it doesn't move games. Marginal Boros/aggro filler when you need to punch through, otherwise cuttable.
Ixidor, Reality Sculptor: Niche disguise-matters payoff. A 3/4 for five that pumps face-down creatures and flips them cheaply is fine but demands a dedicated disguise/cloak shell to shine; null WR leaves the read provisional, but the C+ and heavy-blue cost make it a role-player, not a first-pick.
Duskmantle, House of Shadow: Trap land. A colorless-fixing tapped-mana source whose mill ability is irrelevant in a WR-topped guild-midrange format; 3.6% play rate and D+ say nobody wants it. Skip unless you're forcing a mill gimmick that doesn't exist here.
Worldspine Wurm: Trap. A 12-mana 15/15 is uncastable in a two-color guild format, and the D- grade plus tiny play rate say so — nobody hardcasts this. The death-resilience means nothing when you never reach eleven mana. Sideboard curiosity, never maindeck.
Possibility Storm: Unplayable build-around. A symmetric coin-flip enchantment that does nothing to advance the board and helps opponents as much as you. F grade, sub-2% play — a draft-chaff rare.
Millstone: Trap/sideboard. Mill-two-per-activation does nothing in a grindy midrange format and the D grade plus 2.7% play rate confirm nobody wants it. Never main-deck.
Nyx Weaver: Reasonable BG glue: a 2/3 reach body that blocks disguise 2/2s all day, feeds the graveyard, and buys back your best card late. 53.8% GIH is fine but unexciting — a role-player that enables BG mill/graveyard, not a card you prioritize. Fills a slot rather than wins.
Evolutionary Leap: Niche sac-outlet engine that reads better than it plays — no WR sample and only 14.7% play rate mean most drafters correctly leave it out. Wants a Golgari sacrifice shell to grind card advantage; without one it's a do-nothing enchantment. Provisional B+ is optimistic; treat as a build-around.
Shard of Broken Glass: Filler equipment. A cheap +1/+0 with irrelevant mill; the 3.7% play rate says nobody wants it. Only a consideration in a dedicated self-mill/graveyard shell that needs cheap artifact triggers, otherwise a non-card.
Metalspinner's Puzzleknot: Filler card draw. Two cantrips stapled together, but the -3.6 IWD and sub-50 GIH WR show the tempo loss and life drain outweigh the cards in a grindy format. Only worth it as artifact fodder for sac/evidence decks; otherwise leave it.
Smuggler's Copter: The premium colorless P1P1: a 2-mana 3/3 flyer with looting on attack/block and trivial crew 1. 63.4% GIH, 67.6% OH and near-universal play — it's a bomb. LoL's caveat: only take it if your final deck can actually crew and support the body; don't let it drag you into a crew-less shell.
Consign // Oblivion: Solid playable and a UB workhorse — 56.4% GIH with +3.1 IWD off a 52% play rate. Consign is a clean tempo bounce for two mana; Oblivion's aftermath discard adds late reach and card advantage in the grind. Flexible removal-adjacent value that any Dimir deck wants.
Bishop of the Bloodstained: Filler at best. A 3/3 for five whose ETB drain scales with Vampires you rarely have enough of; without heavy tribal support it's a below-rate body. D+ and 6.9 ALSA — a late speculative playable in dedicated WB Vampires only.
Goblin Warchief: Off-plan trap in MKM — there's no Goblin tribal payoff here, so this is a vanilla 2/2 for three with dead text. D- grade and 10% play rate; leave it in the box.
High Alert: Trap enchantment. Toughness-matters plus untap-your-defenders never assembles in a two-color midrange format — null WR, 4.3% play, D- confirm it's unbuildable here. Skip entirely; there's no MKM archetype that wants it.
Jace, Wielder of Mysteries: Strong planeswalker and a near-auto include in mono-blue-leaning decks: 56.6% GIH, +6.3 IWD, and 2.7 ALSA back a repeatable card-advantage engine whose alt-win clause rarely matters. The triple-blue cost is the only real gate; take it high in any Ux deck.
Syr Konrad, the Grim: Strong black uncommon and a build-around payoff. A 5/4 body alone is fine, but in any sacrifice/mill/aristocrats shell the death-and-graveyard pings snowball fast — 54.4% GIH with +2.9 IWD and an 85% play rate. Take it high in black decks; the mill activation gives reach.
Ranger-Captain of Eos: Premium white two-drop. A 3/3 for three that tutors a 1-drop and can Silence-lock a key turn — 58.9% GIH with a strong 61.9% OH and a 2.4 ALSA make it a first-pick body that overperforms its B- grade. Slam in any white deck.
Hard Evidence: The best blue common — {U} for a 0/3 wall that gums up aggro plus a Clue for later card flow. 56.9% GIH belies how much value it grinds; the 0/3 blocks two-drops all day and the Investigate feeds artifact/detective synergies. Reliable early Azorius/Dimir pickup.
Combine Chrysalis: Trap despite the B grade — the live numbers gut it (47.2% GIH, -4.3 IWD, sub-44% opening-hand). It does nothing the turn it lands and needs a token engine to grind 4/4s, which Simic (GU) rarely assembles fast enough. A do-nothing enchantment in a format that punishes tempo loss; pass it.
Quintorius, Field Historian: Trap gold uncommon. The 45.1% GIH and negative IWD are damning: a 2/4 for five that needs graveyard-leaving triggers this set barely supports, so the Spirit engine rarely turns on. Play only if your WR deck is already deep in recursion.
Laid to Rest: Build-around filler with no home; Human/counter death triggers are too passive for this format. 2% play rate and D+ grade — a sideboard card at best, effectively unplayable.
Monologue Tax: Non-playable rare. A do-nothing Treasure-generator that requires opponents to double-spell and gives you no board — F grade and 4.4% play rate say it all. Never maindeck; this is a pack filler.
Magmaw: Solid midrange body-plus-reach: a 4/4 for five that turns spare permanents into Shock-to-face is fine ping insurance, and 53.9% GIH with a healthy play rate confirms it. The +0.1 IWD shows it's a floor card, not a game-swinger — a good role-player in sacrifice-adjacent red decks.
Mistveil Plains: Filler utility land. The graveyard recursion is cute but the tapland downside drags a mono-white deck's tempo; 50.2% GIH and negative IWD say it's a marginal upgrade at best. Play it only in heavy-white decks that want the recursion, otherwise a basic is fine.
Mentor of the Meek: Solid go-wide engine. The 52% GIH and negative IWD read low because it needs a board of small creatures to draw, but the 92% play rate and 2.4 ALSA say white drafters always run it. Good in token/wide WX shells, mediocre otherwise.
Ghostly Prison: Overrated defensive enchantment: at 51.3% GIH and +0.1 IWD it barely moves games in a grindy format where opponents happily pay the tax or just go wide. C-grade reality despite the mythic frame — a fringe control/ramp sideboard card, not a maindeck priority.
Fabricate: Trap. An F grade and 3.3% play rate confirm it: tutoring for an artifact is worthless when the format has no artifact worth tutoring for. A card-disadvantageous three-mana sorcery. Never play it in Limited.
Show and Tell: Trap in Limited. Symmetric free-put means your opponent also drops their biggest threat, and your pool won't have a payoff worth the risk. D- and 5.8% play — a mythic that's a non-card here; take it for constructed value, not to maindeck.
Tragic Slip: Premium one-mana removal despite the modest 51% GIH WR — that number is dragged down by early-game casts where you only get -1/-1. In a format with abundant combat and death triggers, morbid comes online constantly for a -13/-13 kill-anything. ALSA 2.6 and 75% play rate show it's a real first-few-picks card.
Victimize: The B+ grade flatters it — live 52.3% GIH with only +1.6 IWD makes this a solid-but-not-broken reanimator, not a bomb. High play rate reflects the mythic tag; it needs bodies to sac and targets in the yard. Good in BG grindy decks, a mid pick elsewhere.
Gamble: Trap in Limited. F grade, 12% play rate, no WR data — a one-mana tutor that discards a random card is built for Constructed combo, not a 40-card deck with no must-find target. Ignore it.
Crashing Footfalls: Premium bomb. Pay {G}, suspend, and get eight power of trampling Rhinos for free on turn five — the 62.7% GIH, +10.5 IWD, and 74.8% OH WR are elite, first-pickable numbers. The 1.9 ALSA confirms it goes early; slam it in any green deck.
Tireless Tracker: Bomb-tier value engine. Every land drop makes a Clue and every crack grows it, snowballing card advantage that grinds MKM's midrange out. 60.2% GIH, +6.2 IWD and a 1.5 ALSA confirm it's a first-pick green mythic — take it over almost anything.
Drown in the Loch: Flexible UB counter-or-kill, but it's conditional on graveyard size, so it whiffs early and only 43% of UB decks run it. The +6.9 IWD shows it shines once online, yet the 53.9% GIH marks it as a role-player, not the premium removal the mythic frame suggests. Playable in grindy Dimir.
Field of the Dead: Unplayable here. The seven-differently-named-lands condition is a Constructed engine that never assembles in a two-color guild deck, and it enters tapped for colorless. F grade, ~11% play rate. Ignore it.
Case of the Shattered Pact: Fixing that pretends to be a payoff. The ETB land-tutor smooths a splashy manabase, and 52.6% GIH with positive IWD says the fetch alone earns a slot; the five-color solve rarely fires, so treat it as a two-mana fixer with upside, not a combat trick.
Absolving Lammasu: Solid midrange playable in white. A 5-mana 4/3 flyer with relevant anti-suspect ETB plus a death-payoff (gain 3, suspect a blocker) does honest work. 53% GIH is fine top-end, not a bomb; a good curve-topper you're happy to run.
Assemble the Players: Trap. The -7.0 IWD and 47.9% GIH are damning — it bricks on lands constantly and needs 12+ power-2-or-less creatures to function, which no consistent deck fields. Kenji stands behind it but even he watched it whiff repeatedly. D-; leave it.
Aurelia's Vindicator: The best card in the set. 68.6% GIH, +14.1 IWD, 1.2 ALSA, 97.5% play rate — a 4/2 flying lifelink ward 2 that disguises to hide the cost and flips to exile multiple creatures (returning to YOUR hand if she dies). First pick over everything; LR and LoL both crown it.
Auspicious Arrival: Solid combat trick with a Clue upside. Instant-speed +2/+2 wins a fight and the Investigate replaces the card, so it's rarely a blowout but rarely a blank — 55.4% GIH backs a maindeck slot in white aggro. Good, not premium; the negative IWD reflects trick variance.
Call a Surprise Witness: Solid WX value reanimation. Returns a cheap creature with flying attached — repeatable ETB/tempo in the WU detectives lane the LoL note points to. 53.7% GIH is fine but not exciting; a good playable that gets better the more strong 3-drops you have.
Case of the Gateway Express: Premium white go-wide Case: cheap removal-on-ETB (ping with your board) that trivially solves into a team +1/+0 anthem in any aggressive white deck. 57.7% GIH at a 2.6 ALSA and both LoL/Numot rate it best non-rare Case — "won't wheel." High Boros/Selesnya pick.
Case of the Pilfered Proof: Filler that's usually awkward. As Numot notes, you have to play it before your Detectives to get value, and the solve (three Detectives) is a heavy ask — the -6.0 IWD and 46.5% drawn WR show it whiffs. Only a deeply Detective-committed WU/mono-white build should run it, and even then it's marginal.
Case of the Uneaten Feast: Weak rare. The 46.2% GIH and -5.6 IWD expose it: a one-mana enchantment that does nothing the turn it lands and needs a gain-5-life lifegain shell plus a stocked graveyard to solve. Sideboard/filler outside a dedicated WB lifegain build.
Defenestrated Phantom: Trap despite the flying body. LR flags it as "one of the worst disguise creatures" — 5 mana total to flip into a fragile 3-toughness 4/3, and the -2.8 IWD confirms it underperforms when drawn. Playable ceiling but low priority; cut when you have better sixes.
Delney, Streetwise Lookout: Overrated mythic in the abstract — 51.7% GIH and negative IWD show the 2/2 body underdelivers unless you've built a dedicated small-creature/triggers deck. The 85% play rate is name-tax, not performance. A build-around payoff, not a slam; only prioritize in go-wide white.
Doorkeeper Thrull: Trap despite the rare frame. A 1/2 flash flyer whose static hoses ETB triggers is the wrong effect for MKM — LR notes it doesn't even stop disguise reveals. 51% GIH and negative IWD confirm it's a marginal body; only a fringe playable in flyer-defense decks.
Due Diligence: Role-player aura. A two-creature +2/+2 vigilance swing has upside on a wide board, but auras carry two-for-one risk and the 51.9% GIH with negative IWD marks it fringe. Playable in dedicated go-wide white, a cut in most decks.
Essence of Antiquity: Role-player wall. A 1/10 that flips from disguise to save your team with hexproof/untap is a fine defensive combat trick and blocker, but a below-water GIH WR and -3.4 IWD mark it as a slow, situational body. Playable filler in grindy decks.
Forum Familiar: Filler. A {W} 1/1 whose disguise flip bounces your own permanent for a counter — cute value but slow and low-impact; the -4.8 IWD and sub-50% OH say it clogs your deck more than it helps. Only playable in a dedicated ETB/blink white build, otherwise a sideboard card.
Griffnaut Tracker: Below-average filler. A 3/2 flyer for four is playable evasion in white, but the negative IWD and 51.6% GIH mark it as a curve-filler, not a pick you prioritize. The graveyard-exile ETB is minor incidental hate. Late playable when you need bodies.
Haazda Vigilante: Solid Boros top-end. A 4/4 for five that repeatedly grows your small attackers on ETB and every swing — exactly the go-wide payoff RW wants, and Numot calls it one of the best top-ends in the beatdown deck. 54.8% GIH backs it; the negative IWD is just curve-topper noise.
Inside Source: Premium white common and a WB/white-aggro engine. Three mana buys a 1/1 plus a 2/2 Detective token (two bodies, go-wide fuel) with a repeatable Detective pump. 57.6% GIH, 92% play rate — a slam early pick that anchors the token plan.
Karlov Watchdog: Quietly strong white uncommon. A 3/2 vigilance with an anthem-on-attack rider that rewards white's go-wide plan, and the face-up hate is real vs disguise decks. 55.6% GIH backs it as a reliable playable — take it as a solid two-drop-curve filler for aggressive white.
Krovod Haunch: Playable-if-needed one-drop equipment that plays like a slow value card — the +2/+0, the lifegain sac, and the two-Dog death trigger add up but never fast. 53.4% GIH is decent yet the -3.1 IWD flags it as filler that clogs draws. Fine deep in an aggressive white deck, cuttable otherwise.
Make Your Move: Premium flexible removal — a key maindeck answer. Kills artifacts, enchantments, and any power-4+ threat (including big disguise flips and a huge share of MKM rares), so LoL and LR both want 1+ maindecked. The 54.7% GIH is understated by how many games it just doesn't draw a target; take it as your interaction.
Makeshift Binding: Premium white common removal. O-Ring on a creature plus 2 life — the experts unanimously call it a first-pick, Ethan's #1 common, and the extra value beats the ward-2 downside. 58.5% GIH and 92.9% play rate: take it early, always run it.
Marketwatch Phantom: Serviceable white two-drop that gains flying whenever a small creature enters — a fine go-wide/aggro body that can push evasive damage. 55.4% GIH with strong OH (57.5) confirms it curves out well early, though the -1.5 IWD shows it's a play-early card, not a topdeck. Solid Boros/Selesnya role-player.
Museum Nightwatch: Solid common and a white staple — 55.3% GIH at a huge 82% play rate. The die-into-a-2/2-Detective ETB gives real two-for-one value, and disguise lets you sandbag it as a ward-2 blocker or an ambush. Sticky, flexible, and enables Detective payoffs; a reliable mid-pick.
Neighborhood Guardian: Premium go-wide enabler. The 2.7 ALSA and 91% play rate tell the story: a two-drop anthem-on-a-stick that pumps as your small creatures flood the board. Strong in WB/WU pint-size and Detective decks; the OH/GD split shows it's best deployed early to snowball.
No Witnesses: Solid but swingy WW wrath, not a slam. The catch LR flags: the opponent usually has the most creatures and Clues back, so it's a weak-ish board reset. Still a real board-in-a-can for controlling white decks — 52% GIH reflects the awkwardness of a symmetric-ish sweeper.
Not on My Watch: Trap despite the exile. LoL nails it: this is reactive removal in a proactive color — you can't exile an attacker when you're the beatdown, so the timing fights white's plan. The 55.5% GIH is inflated by good white decks around it; treat as a mediocre role-player, not premium removal.
Novice Inspector: The #1 common in the format — a one-mana 1/2 that investigates, i.e. a Thraben Inspector reprint. 59.5% GIH and 62.7% OH on a WHITE one-drop is absurd; all three guides call it never-cut, splashable, first-pickable. Take it early and always play it.
On the Job: Breakout uncommon and a white go-wide win-con — 'cast On the Job, win.' The early D+ grade is superseded; it's a pseudo-Overrun that also draws a Clue and ties Boros/Azorius wide decks together. 55.7% GIH understates the ceiling; prioritize it if you're building around creatures.
Perimeter Enforcer: Premium aggressive two-drop. A 1/1 flyer with lifelink that snowballs off every Detective ETB/flip — all three experts flag it as a top WU/Boros uncommon that's hard to cut. 57.8% GIH and 60.3% OH confirm the aggressive-start payoff; P1-worthy in detective decks.
Sanctuary Wall: Weak. A 0/4 defender whose tap-and-stun ability costs {2}{W} and stuns itself too, making it a clunky, mana-hungry speed bump. D grade, 23.9% play, negative IWD — near-unplayable outside a dedicated control shell that badly needs to stall.
Seasoned Consultant: Good aggressive two-drop backbone for WU/white. A 1/3 blocks early and turns into a 3/3 attacker once you're going wide, and 55.1% GIH with 56.8% opening-hand WR (per LoL/Numot, you want it on turn two) confirms it as a cornerstone body. Prioritize in go-wide white decks.
Tenth District Hero: Bomb-tier two-drop. 1.4 ALSA, 92.8% play, +3.3 IWD, A- grade — a 2/3 for two that scales into a 4/4 vigilance and eventually a 5/5 lord granting indestructible. Curves early, wins late, never a dead card. First-pick white gold.
Unyielding Gatekeeper: Premium white common and a top-tier pick — the numbers scream it: +2.8 IWD, ALSA 1.7, 92% play rate, 58% GIH. A cheap disguise body that flips to exile ANY nonland permanent (bounce-recur your own, hard-exile theirs). Flexible removal on a creature; take it highly.
Wrench: Filler equipment/Clue. The -3.2 IWD and 22.8% play rate say it's slow and clunky — the tap ability costs too much and the card-draw sac mode is a consolation prize. C-; a late-pick body-buff for aggressive white only if you're short on playables.
Agency Outfitter: Trap build-around. The 4/3 flyer for six only pays off if you drafted Magnifying Glass and/or Thinking Cap, which almost nobody does — hence 17.4% play rate and a below-water 50.4% GIH. As a vanilla flyer it's overcosted; leave it unless the pieces are in your pool.
Behind the Mask: Trap. Two weak modes stapled together — a temporary 4/3 animation that gets worse if you pay the evidence cost — and the 3.9% play rate plus sub-50 GIH confirm it's unplayable. Leave it in the box.
Benthic Criminologists: Filler five-drop. A 4/5 body is fine but the sac-artifact-to-draw rider is redundant with Clues and rarely fires; LR calls it "just bad." 53% GIH on a 17% play rate is a late-clue-deck body only — a curve-filler, not a pick.
Bubble Smuggler: Disguise beater that flips into a 6/5 for {5}{U} — a fine curve-filler with a combat-trick blowout upside, but the flip cost is steep and it does nothing else. 53.2% GIH is playable, not exciting; a mid-to-late Azorius/Simic body when you need bodies.
Burden of Proof: Solid playable, best in a Detective deck. Flash makes it a combat trick — pumps your Detective +2/+2 or shrinks their attacker to a 1/1 that can't block. The 52.7% GIH is fine but the ceiling needs Detectives; a versatile role-player for WU rather than a slam.
Candlestick: Marginal role-player. A one-mana Equipment that adds surveil-on-attack and cashes out for a card, but the +1/+1 body-tax and 2-to-equip make it slow; 50.4% GIH and 18% play mark it as a synergy filler for surveil/Clue decks, not a maindeck staple.
Case of the Filched Falcon: UR artifact build-around, niche. One mana to investigate now, then later turn any noncreature artifact into a 4/4 flyer — oppressive with a spare Clue or Geardrake. 53% GIH is fine but it's a synergy card, best in the dedicated UR artifacts deck LoL flags.
Case of the Ransacked Lab: Build-around trap for spells-matter, an archetype MKM doesn't reliably support. Casting four instants/sorceries in a turn to solve is a fantasy at Limited — F grade and 1.7% play confirm it's unplayable. Skip.
Cold Case Cracker: A clean, reliable UW/UG defensive common: 3/3 flyer for four that leaves a Clue when it dies, so it trades up and replaces itself. 55.4% GIH and 84% play rate confirm the perfect blocker-that-cantrips statline. Solid mid-priority pick for control decks.
Conspiracy Unraveler: Mediocre top-end. A 6/6 flier is a fine finisher, but seven mana is a lot and the free-cast evidence ability rarely comes online in Limited; 51.0% GIH is just a big flier's floor. Playable as a curve-topper in slow blue decks, never a priority.
Coveted Falcon: Trap rare. A 1/4 flyer with symmetric-downside combo text that reads better than it plays; the 51.9% GIH and -1.4 IWD undercut its 74.8% play rate. Evasive body is fine but the C grade is honest — a marginal blue playable, not a bomb.
Crimestopper Sprite: Downgraded end-of-format: a 2/2 flyer that taps (and stuns, if you pay collect evidence 6) on ETB — the stun is rarely online, so it's usually just a vanilla flyer with a Falter. Both Numot and LR moved DOWN, preferring Forensic Researcher. Playable Azorius filler, no longer a priority.
Cryptic Coat: Bomb — first-pick material. 63.2% GIH, +10.2 IWD, ALSA 1.5, near-94% play rate: the numbers scream premium and all three guides agree (LR: A+, one of the best Limited cards LSV has seen). Recastable, makes an evasive ward-2 body every turn, and transfers unblockable to anything. Take it over almost everything.
Curious Inquiry: Fringe Aura payoff. Numot's right that it's sneaky-good on a face-down/hexproof body that can't be removed in response, generating repeated Clues — but the 50.5% GIH says it's card-disadvantage bait against removal. A UR/UW investigate-synergy pick, not a general playable.
Deduce: Solid blue card-flow that plays better than its C grade — LR calls it a "really pushed" cantrip. Two mana to draw plus bank a Clue keeps the grind going and feeds artifact/Clue synergies. Fine playable; double Deduce lets you hold up counter-mana comfortably.
Dramatic Accusation: Playable pseudo-removal that locks a creature down and can shuffle it away for {U}{U}. 53.7% GIH is fine but the big gd-vs-oh gap (55.3 vs 51.1) shows it's better as a mid-game answer than an opener. Numot cooled on it; a serviceable blue role-player, not a priority.
Eliminate the Impossible: Serviceable blue combat trick / Clue-maker — the -2/-0 to all opposing creatures blows out attacks or shrinks a blocker while cantripping via investigate, and the un-suspect clause is minor upside. 54.2% GIH on 61% play is fine role-player value, not premium; take it middle of the pack.
Exit Specialist: One of the format's better uncommons. Bounce on the disguise flip is pseudo-removal that also blows out their face-down mana investment, and the evasive 2/1 body applies pressure early — 56.9% GIH, +2.0 IWD, 90% play rate. Take it high in any blue deck.
Fae Flight: Situational combat trick / evasion enabler. Flash hexproof plus flying can steal a race or blowout a removal spell, but a sub-50 OH WR and -1.2 IWD show it's a do-nothing when behind. Fringe blue playable for tempo/flyer decks only.
Forensic Gadgeteer: Build-around rare that underdelivers: it wants a dense artifact/Clue deck to snowball Investigate triggers and cost reduction, but 51.9% GIH and +0.1 IWD show that shell rarely comes together. A 2/3 body for three otherwise. Speculative Izzet/artifacts payoff, not a reliable pick.
Forensic Researcher: Rising star — take it high. Numot flags it went UP significantly end-of-format: the untap/tap toolbox works even without collect-evidence synergies, and it enables ramp/fixing off the untap. 55% GIH with positive IWD and 73% play rate. Prioritize over Crimestopper Sprite; strong blue two-drop.
Furtive Courier: Solid blue two-drop-plus. A 3/2 that loots on attack and goes unblockable when you sac an artifact — strong in Clue/artifact decks where the evasion turns on. 53.5% GIH and 68% play confirm a reliable role-player; the looting keeps it relevant late.
Hotshot Investigators: Role-player top-end in blue. Six mana for a 4/4 with a soft bounce (only Clues if you bounce your own) is slow, and the 6.8 ALSA plus 34% play rate mark it as a fringe inclusion. Serviceable tempo in a pinch, not a card you prioritize.
Intrude on the Mind: Premium blue card advantage — draw a fistful plus a scaling flying Thopter, exactly what Ux control wants. 58.5% GIH, +5.1 IWD, and near-universal play confirm the ceiling. B+ is right; a high pick for any blue deck, especially control mirrors.
Jaded Analyst: LSV's favorite Simic blocker: a 3/2 defender that becomes a 3/2 vigilance attacker once you draw a second card, so it walls early then pivots. Numot's high on it, LR says skip it in aggressive/removal-flush decks. 52.3% GIH is modest — a good role-player specifically in slow UG/UW.
Living Conundrum: Trap. LSV loved the mill-yourself-out combo conceptually but it never worked — 46.6% GIH and a dismal 42.3% OH WR confirm a 2/5 that does nothing until your library is empty. A defensive blocker at absolute best; effectively unplayable.
Lost in the Maze: Solid blue tempo/protection tool. Numot loves it — flash tap-down plus hexproof for your team protects a key creature mid-combat and swings races; the big GD-over-OH gap (58.2 vs 51.5) marks it as a reactive card that shines when drawn into a board. Good playable.
Mistway Spy: Fine one-drop flyer with disguise flexibility, but the flip payoff (Investigate on combat damage) is marginal. 52.0% GIH is filler-tier; you're mostly getting a {U} 1/1 flyer or a {3} 2/2. Playable evasive body in Azorius detectives, low priority.
Out Cold: Premium tempo — draft multiples in blue. Uncounterable tap-two plus a stun counter plus Investigate for three mana is a huge combat swing that replaces itself; all guides converged upward ("fantastic," "amazing"). 55.3% GIH with the drawn WR strong. Best in Simic (GU) tempo; grab every copy.
Proft's Eidetic Memory: Near-bomb build-around. +5.4 IWD, 2.4 ALSA, 85% play — this enchantment replaces itself and turns any extra draw into a fistful of counters, which cheap Clues/investigate trigger constantly. A premium blue engine; take it highly wherever you're in blue.
Projektor Inspector: Solid blue-tempo common and a Detective payoff. A 3/2 for three that loots on every Detective ETB/flip is real card selection in the UW/UB detective decks. 56% GIH, 82% play rate, positive IWD — a comfortable early-to-mid playable.
Reasonable Doubt: Format-defining Simic tempo counter — Force Spike plus a suspect rider for two mana. 56.3% GIH with strong opening-hand numbers shows it plays well early; LR calls it a core UG piece. Prioritize in tempo/spells blue but cut extras in removal-heavy builds. Solid-to-good.
Reenact the Crime: Bad. 43.3% GIH, -4.3 IWD, 6.4% play rate, D- grade, and Numot's blunt "not very good" — a triple-blue instant that only hits cards that entered a graveyard THIS turn is far too conditional. Don't play it.
Steamcore Scholar: Premium rare and a near-slam in blue. A 2/2 flying vigilance that draws two and usually keeps both (discard is easy to dodge with an instant/sorcery or flier) is card advantage on an evasive body — 61.0% GIH, +6.7 IWD, 90% play rate. First-pick caliber.
Unauthorized Exit: Solid Simic/tempo bounce. Return-any-nonland plus surveil 1 blows out tricks and resets a flipped disguise creature at four mana; 55.7% GIH and positive IWD back LR's premium-tempo read. A flexible, better-than-average blue common.
Agency Coroner: Weak sac outlet on an overpriced 3/6 for five; the {2}{B} draw engine is too slow and only 7.4% of decks bother. D+, negative OH, 7.9 ALSA — black being the worst color, this is bottom-of-pool filler. Skip outside a dedicated sacrifice deck.
Alley Assailant: Solid role-player, best via disguise. Cast face-down as a 2/2 ward, then flip for a Falter-style 3-life drain and a 3/3 body — a real tempo-and-reach two-for-one. 53% GIH with a flat IWD; the enters-tapped downside caps it. A fine black common that rewards patient play.
Barbed Servitor: Solid aggressive engine. Indestructible plus suspect means it swings unblocked and draws a card each hit, and its damage reflects onto the opponent — a resilient threat black wants. 51.1% GIH is modest but the 2.7 ALSA and 73% play show it earns its slot as a self-suspecting card-advantage attacker.
Basilica Stalker: Role-player black flyer. A 3/4 flyer with disguise flexibility and incidental life/surveil is a fine curve-topper, but 52% GIH and a neutral IWD say it's replaceable filler. Play it when your black deck needs bodies in the air; don't reach.
Case of the Stashed Skeleton: Downgraded by end of format — Numot flipped from 'fantastic' to 'kind of bad' because the 2/1 suspected Skeleton can't block and is ignorable in a board-centric format. Still 57.1% GIH (tutor upside is real), but the B+ overrates it now. A good, not great, black two-drop.
Cerebral Confiscation: Trap on early hype — Numot rated it a top black common then publicly walked it back by day 3. Sorcery-speed discard is weak in a creature-combat format; 48.3% GIH, 7.3% play, D grade confirm. Leave it in the sideboard.
Deadly Cover-Up: Powerful but archetype-locked wrath. A 5-mana BB Damnation is a bomb in a Dimir control shell built to survive to it, but 'effectively a mulligan' in aggro — never run it there. The 59.0% GIH reflects control decks only; the exile bonus rarely matters. Draft it when you're the control deck, not by default.
Extract a Confession: Premium black removal — black's best common. An efficient edict that bypasses ward 2 and fuels collect evidence; all three experts rank it above Murder on 17Lands. 56.1% GIH and +3.0 IWD confirm it. Take it early in any black deck.
Festerleech: Sneaky-good black one-drop: a {B} 1/1 that pumps to a 3/3 attacker on demand and mills to feed graveyard/collect-evidence. 55.4% GIH and a strong 58.7% OH earn its B- — an aggressive early play in Golgari/Dimir grave decks that trades up and closes. Solid role-player.
Homicide Investigator: Premium two-drop — near-bomb. A 1B 2/2 that Investigates on any nontoken creature death (once/turn) is a trivially-triggered card-advantage engine (LR: A-). 57.6% GIH, +5.5 IWD, ALSA 2.0 confirm it fuels the grind. Snaps up in any black deck, elite in BR/BG sacrifice.
Hunted Bonebrute: Excellent black threat. +6.4 IWD and 58.5% GIH on a 6/2 menace for three that also drains 3 on death and disguises to dodge sorcery-speed removal — the Dog downside is minor. B+ and 87% play; one of black's best commons-slot beaters.
Illicit Masquerade: Trap. 48.2% GIH, negative IWD and a D+ grade — the impostor-counter reanimation loop is too cute and fragile, needing your creatures to die on cue. A build-around that doesn't pay off; leave it out of maindecks.
It Doesn't Add Up: Overcosted reanimation. Five mana to return one creature that can't block is too slow — 49.0% GIH and terrible 45.2% OH confirm it clogs your hand early. D+; only a niche BG grindy include, otherwise a sideboard card.
Lead Pipe: Below-replacement equipment. +2/+0, a minor drain on the wearer's death, and a sac-to-draw make it a value card on paper, but 50.3% GIH and -1.9 IWD on 17% play say it's too slow and card-disadvantageous in practice. Fringe filler for artifact-sac decks only.
Leering Onlooker: Banger black uncommon — 'Lingering Souls on defense.' A 1/3 flier that recurs from the graveyard into two more fliers gives grindy value and is a perfect surveil/mill target; 55.1% GIH with a strong 85% play rate. High pick in black grind decks.
Long Goodbye: Premium cheap removal — black's best. Uncounterable, kills MV≤3 for two, crushing cheap disguise flips; 56.8% GIH, +4.2 IWD and 86% play rate. Caveat noted by every expert: it whiffs on flipped MV-4+ creatures, so it gets awkward late, but still a top black pick.
Macabre Reconstruction: Grindy recursion: returns up to two creatures, and gets cheap when a creature hit your yard this turn. The gd_wr (53.8) beating OH shows it's a topdeck value card, not an early play; -0.4 IWD marks it filler. A fine late-game engine in Golgari/sacrifice, low pick priority.
Massacre Girl, Known Killer: Bomb. 2BB 4/4 menace that gives your team wither and draws whenever their creatures die small — she punishes both blocking and their removal simultaneously (LR: A). 56.7% GIH, ALSA 1.5, 85% play. Format-warping board control; first-pick her.
Murder: Premium unconditional removal, contested by the guides. Instant-speed destroy-any-creature is exactly what removal-scarce MKM wants, and the ward-2 tax barely dents it; LR/Ethan dock it as passive but the 55% GIH and +2.5 IWD say it's a clean, high-priority answer, best in UB/BG control.
Nightdrinker Moroii: Contested uncommon that the retro read cools on — a 4-mana 4/2 flyer that costs you 3 life, and disguise mitigates the drain but not the fragile toughness. 53% GIH is fine, but LoL leans to the low read and rates Slimy Dualist above it. A serviceable evasive beater, not a priority.
Outrageous Robbery: Big split between opener and drawn (48.3 OH vs 55.9 gd) — this is a mid-to-late card-advantage engine, not something you want turn one. 53.1% GIH is solid for a flexible X-spell that fixes its own colors. A fine role-player for grindy black decks; C+ is fair.
Persuasive Interrogators: A fine top-end body with a poison side-plan you'll rarely close on: a 5/6 for six that investigates, and each Clue you crack gives the opponent two poison. 53.9% GIH and +2.3 IWD ride mostly on the raw stats; the poison kill is a novelty. Reasonable curve-topper in Clue-heavy black decks.
Polygraph Orb: Trap. A 5-mana Read the Bones with a slow, weak drain ability — 'way too slow, too weak,' F even in black. The +3.1 IWD flatters a card the 15.6% play rate says nobody keeps in. Skip it.
Presumed Dead: Fringe combat trick / value gimmick. +2/+0 with a die-and-return-suspected rider can save a creature or push damage, but 52.3% GIH and a 36% play rate mark it as unreliable filler. Only for aggressive suspect-synergy decks; usually a sideboard card.
Repeat Offender: Filler two-drop. A 2/1 that either becomes an evasive menace attacker or slowly grows via +1/+1 counters, but the {2}{B} activations are mana-hungry and it can't block once suspected. 51.7% GIH and C- — a marginal aggressive body in a weak color. Playable, uninspiring.
Rot Farm Mortipede: Filler, essentially a BG-graveyard build-around. A 3/4 for four is a fine body, but the pump/menace/lifelink only fires when creature cards leave your graveyard — an engine most decks don't run. ALSA 7.2 and 21% play rate mark it as a late niche pick. Skip unless deep in reanimator/recursion.
Slice from the Shadows: Strong flexible removal. Scalable -X/-X that can't be countered — crucially it sidesteps ward-2 disguise, one of the doctrine's premium-removal traits — and kills anything given enough mana. 54.2% GIH and 78% play make it a reliable early black pick.
Slimy Dualleech: Solid black uncommon. A 2/4 wall that hands out +1/+0 and deathtouch each combat trades up all day and blocks aggro cleanly. Positive IWD and 63% play rate — a dependable, unflashy defensive playable that quietly wins races on the ground.
Snarling Gorehound: Conditional one-drop with menace and a surveil engine. Strong 57.0% OH shows it's a fine aggressive opener, but the gd drop-off and Numot's note flag that the power-2 trigger fires less than you'd hope. A serviceable black one-drop for small-creature decks, not a build-around.
Soul Enervation: Efficient flexible black interaction — flash, -4/-4 kills most things at instant speed, plus recurring drain when creatures leave your yard. 54.3% GIH, +1.9 IWD, and 78% play on a 3.7 ALSA make it a strong WB/black playable; take it fairly high as removal.
Toxin Analysis: Solid trick with a Clue. Deathtouch lets a small creature kill anything in combat while lifelink swings races, and the Investigate refunds the card — 53.9% GIH with positive IWD. A fine flexible maindeck trick in black, not a priority pick.
Undercity Eliminator: Solid removal-on-a-body. A 5-mana 3/3 that sacs a token/creature to exile theirs — LoL undersells it as "just a 3/3," but the +2.0 IWD and 56.2% GD WR show the exile ETB earns its keep in grindy sac decks. Good playable, especially with fodder.
Unscrupulous Agent: Good pedigree hand disruption on a body: {1}{B} 1/1 that exiles a card from the opponent's hand on ETB. 55.3% GIH with +1.9 IWD is genuinely fine — LR notes black's weakness suppressed it, so it flows later than it should. A solid tempo/disruption two-drop for Dimir/Rakdos.
Vein Ripper: Format-defining bomb — the triple-black cost is the only caveat. A 6/5 flyer with a sacrifice-ward that drains 2 on every creature death wins the game on cast (Numot: "broken"; LR: A+). 63.6% GIH, +12.9 IWD, ALSA 1.5. If you can support BBB, take it over almost anything.
Anzrag's Rampage: Unplayable. A five-mana artifact-wrath-plus-cascade that needs an artifact-heavy board to do anything and blows up your own Clues; F grade, 1% play. Leave it.
Bolrac-Clan Basher: Solid red uncommon. Double strike plus trample makes it a removal-magnet threat, and disguise lets you deploy on curve and flip for a surprise blowout. 54% GIH, 80% play rate — a reliable Boros/Gruul top-end you're glad to run.
Case of the Burning Masks: Premium-adjacent red removal: three damage on ETB with card-advantage upside on solve, and LoL notes the extra value beats the ward eval. 55.0% GIH is good for a removal spell; take it highly in any red deck as a two-for-one Shock+.
Case of the Crimson Pulse: A strong Rakdos card-advantage engine: rummage two immediately, then once you empty your hand it refills two every upkeep — LoL says it does Connecting the Dots' job better. 53.4% GIH with a big 76% play rate; the -1.2 IWD reflects it wanting an empty-hand aggressive shell. Good in RB.
Caught Red-Handed: Filler tempo/finisher. Five mana for a one-turn Threaten with menace is a lot; it's a niche alpha-strike enabler, not removal, and the 51.3% GIH with negative IWD and 8.9% play rate mark it fringe. Sideboard-y at best.
The Chase Is On: Middling red trick. +3/+0 first strike wins combat and investigates for a card back, softening the tempo cost — but 55.4% GIH with negative IWD says it's a fine-not-great combat trick. A serviceable aggressive-red playable, not a priority.
Concealed Weapon: Trap-ish equipment: +3/+0 for {1}{R} equip, "disgusting" on a token or 1-power flyer (Numot), but the -3.5 IWD and 51.3% GIH show it underdelivers when you don't have the right body. Only take it if you're heavy on evasive/token creatures; otherwise a low Boros/Izzet playable.
Connecting the Dots: Trap — the rare case where retro says ignore the dumpster data AND still "never play it" is right. LoL calls it a narrow Rakdos (RB) card that Case of the Crimson Pulse does better; LR grades it D/F for too much setup. -7.3 IWD. Pass it.
Convenient Target: Fringe aggro Aura. Suspect-plus-pump pushes a beater through as a menacing attacker with graveyard recursion, but it's card-disadvantage that dies to removal; 52.4% GIH and -3.0 IWD flag it as replaceable filler for go-wide red decks only.
Cornered Crook: Solid red removal-on-a-body when you have artifacts to feed it — a 5/4 for five that sacs an artifact to Shock any target (and can go face, beating Undercity Eliminator per LoL). Ward-2 blunts it as removal, so 54% GIH; best in Clue/artifact-heavy red decks.
Crime Novelist: Payoff for artifact-sac that mostly does nothing without the shell — 49.9% GIH and -2.8 IWD show the 1/3 body is inert alone. A synergy piece for BR/Rx sacrifice, filler otherwise. Only prioritize if you're deep in Clues/Treasures.
Demand Answers: Below-average card draw — Draw two for {1}{R} is fine, but the additional cost of saccing an artifact or discarding stings, and 50.8% GIH with -2.7 IWD on 26% play confirm it's card-neutral filler. Playable in artifact-rich decks that want to enable other cards, otherwise skip.
Expedited Inheritance: Sideboard/trap. A symmetric card-advantage enchantment that's clunky and slow in Limited — F grade, 1.8% play rate, and null WR from lack of play all agree nobody wants it. Skip.
Expose the Culprit: Sideboard trap. Needs 8+ disguise creatures to do anything and still underwhelms — Numot says cut it. 47.1% GIH, -4.6 IWD and a 7% play rate make it one of the worst red cards; don't run it.
Felonious Rage: Underrated red trick: {R} for +2/+0 and haste that leaves a 2/2 detective if the creature dies — so it wins combat AND replaces itself on a trade. LR moved it UP end-of-format (LSV played multiples). 55.6% GIH; it flows because it "looks bad." A quietly strong aggressive Boros/Rakdos pickup.
Frantic Scapegoat: Solid aggressive one-drop. A hasty 1/1 that self-suspects for menace and can shuffle the suspect onto later attackers is real early pressure in a go-wide red deck. 55.2% GIH and 58% opening-hand WR (it wants to be in your opener). A fine aggro enabler, filler in slower decks.
Fugitive Codebreaker: Premium red two-drop. A 2/1 prowess haste that's fine on curve and becomes a graveyard-fueled loot-3 disguise engine in spells-matter decks. 2.1 ALSA, 90% play, B+ — aggressive floor, high ceiling; take it early in any red deck.
Galvanize: Good-not-great red removal — the preview hype settled to "average" across all three guides. Four total mana to reliably kill a disguised 2/2, and Shock does the job for one less. 56% GIH and 90% play rate say it's a fine maindeck trick; just don't overrate it P1.
Gearbane Orangutan: Flexible common: a 2/2 reach that either pops an artifact or grows to a 4/4 by eating your own. 52.3% GIH is middling — the artifact-destroy mode is often dead, so it's a role-player. Fine in red decks with Clues/Treasures to sac; unremarkable otherwise.
Goblin Maskmaker: A disguise-deck enabler, not a maindeck creature: the 1/2 makes your face-down spells cheaper only when it attacks. LR flags it UP specifically in disguise-dense builds (a build-around at two-plus copies). The 58.7% OH vs 50.7% GD split shows it's an early-curve card that fades late — role-player in dedicated disguise decks.
Harried Dronesmith: Role-player. A 2/3 that spits out a hasty 1/1 flier each combat is steady chip damage and fuels artifact-sacrifice synergies, but the token dies each turn so it's just okay — 52.2% GIH, negative IWD despite 82% play rate. Solid filler body in red, especially UR artifacts.
Incinerator of the Guilty: Bomb. A 6/6 flying trampler that near-always connects, then wraths their board via collect evidence — it flat ends games. 58.6% GIH, +5.2 IWD, 1.3 ALSA and an A grade: first-pick, take-over-anything red mythic.
Innocent Bystander: Aggressive 2/1 goblin whose Investigate trigger (take 3+ damage) is a minor consolation on a trade. 53.1% GIH and a -3.2 IWD mark it as an early curve-filler, not a value card — you play it to attack, not to draw. Fine Boros/Gruul two-drop filler.
Knife: Filler equipment, mostly cuttable. First strike plus +1/+0 on your turn is minor, and the sac-to-draw is expensive (2 to draw, 2 to equip). 48.1% GIH, -5.5 IWD, 20% play rate all say it underperforms. Only a dedicated aggro/first-strike deck wants it; usually leave it.
Krenko, Baron of Tin Street: Bomb in artifact/Goblin decks. A 3/3 haste for three that snowballs off every artifact dying — Clues, Thopters, Servitors — pumping Goblins and spawning more. A- grade, +4.4 IWD, 90% play; a first-pick engine especially in UR/RB sacrifice.
Krenko's Buzzcrusher: Strong red rare and near-slam — a 4/4 flying trampler for four that also blows up a nonbasic land is great tempo plus disruption. ALSA 2.0, 87% play rate, B grade; take it high in any red deck as a clean evasive beater with upside.
Lamplight Phoenix: Excellent red rare — a recurring 3/3 flyer that keeps coming back via collect evidence 4. 59.3% GIH, +3.9 IWD, near-90% play, A- grade all align: LR warns not to cast it under 4 evidence but the ceiling is a relentless evasive threat. High pick in any red deck.
Offender at Large: Solid disguise beater: play a 2/2 ward 2 on turn three, flip later into a 5/4 with a +2/+0 pump, or hardcast the 5/4 on five. 55.6% GIH and 64% play make it a dependable red common curve-filler with combat flexibility; a fine mid-pick.
Person of Interest: The most powerful red common by 17Lands. Four mana for a suspected 2/2 plus a 2/2 Detective token is two bodies of pressure and detective-tribal fuel — 58.2% GIH, 59% OH WR, 82% play rate. High pick in any red deck.
Pyrotechnic Performer: Premium red rare — LSV's best red card by win rate. A 3/2 disguise for two that burns the opponent for its power every time you flip a creature; 59.8% GIH and +4.7 IWD. Aggressive, snowballs with disguise, and always great. Take it early.
Reckless Detective: Underrated blue-white... no, red engine: a {1}{R} 0/3 that blocks early garbage, then filters cards and swings as a 2/3 by sac'ing a Clue or discarding. 58.6% GIH with a huge 62.8% OH — the "nut curve" partner to Novice Inspector (Numot/LR). High-priority Izzet/artifacts two-drop; don't over-stack early plays.
Red Herring: Format-flip card — good only in dedicated aggro/sac shells. Numot mocked it then ran 3-4 copies; LR moved it up. A hasty 2/2 that must attack and cashes in for a card is real in RB/Crook sacrifice or pump decks, mediocre elsewhere. 55.4% GIH reflects the good homes; contextual.
Rubblebelt Braggart: Late filler. A vanilla 5/5 for five whose only text is self-suspect for a marginal alpha-strike; 51.7% GIH and 7.1 ALSA mark it as replacement-level top-end you take late when short on bodies.
Shock: Premium red common — the best in the color per every guide. One mana instant that kills the format's ~46% two-drops and ambushes face-down 2/2s, with color flexibility that keeps UR/RW open (Ben took it over Helix at P4). 57% GIH, never sideboard it out. First-pickable.
Suspicious Detonation: Weak removal unless you're in the artifact-sac shell that pays two. The pay-5 mode is unplayable — LR says aim for zero — and the 51.1% GIH with -1.9 IWD reflects how often you're paying full price. C-; a niche include for dedicated red-sac decks only.
Vengeful Tracker: Punisher two-drop that's better than it looks in MKM — a 2/2 that pings for 2 whenever an opponent cracks a Clue or sacs an artifact, and this format is full of Clues. 54.5% GIH and 83% play back it as a solid aggressive red common; take it as good filler.
Aftermath Analyst: Role-player with landfall upside. The mill-three ETB fuels graveyard synergies and the land-reanimation sac is a real ramp/value payoff in the right deck — 53.2% GIH is dead-average, telling you it's fine everywhere but exciting only in Golgari/self-mill. Solid midrange filler.
Airtight Alibi: Fringe green trick. Flash +2/+2, untap and hexproof can blow out combat and un-suspect your creature, but 53.8% GIH on a 26.6% play rate marks it as situational filler. A sideboard-y trick; run it only if short on playables.
Analyze the Pollen: Efficient green toolbox: {G} to fetch a basic, or grab any creature/land if you collect evidence 8 late. 54.9% GIH with a smoothing role — fixes mana early and finds your best threat late. B-; a flexible, always-playable green card that keeps GW/Simic decks running.
Archdruid's Charm: Solid flexible playable — a green Swiss-army knife. Fetch a creature/land, fight-plus-counter for removal, or blow up an artifact/enchantment; the fight mode makes it real removal. GGG is demanding but 56.9% GIH with 75% play and ALSA 3.2 show it delivers. Prioritize in green-base decks.
Audience with Trostani: Weak build-around. LR nails it — you almost never have enough differently-named tokens to draw more than one card, making this a three-mana cantrip-plus-Plant most games. 54.6% GIH is inflated by the few token-heavy GW decks; skip unless you're flooding tokens.
Axebane Ferox: Bomb-adjacent green rare and a first-pick. A 2GG 4/4 with deathtouch AND haste AND ward-Collect-Evidence-4 is often literally unkillable early — the eye-popping +5.5 IWD, 60% OH WR and ALSA 1.8 confirm it. Slam it.
Bite Down on Crime: Re-evaluated up: fight-removal that bypasses ward 2 and collects evidence, and even small CE inclusions make it good. 57.2% GIH validates the retro read over the weak preview. Requires a creature on board but that's easy in green; a solid green removal pick.
Case of the Locked Hothouse: High-variance ramp payoff with huge range — extra lands now, then a top-of-library card-advantage engine once you hit seven lands. LoL: "sometimes dead, sometimes wins games nothing else could." 56% GIH and +2.8 IWD on 82% play say it converts well in slower green decks; a strong pick in ramp-y Simic/Golgari.
Case of the Trampled Garden: Solid green uncommon. Two +1/+1 counters up front is fine value, and once solved (easy in a creature deck) it's a repeatable counter-plus-trample engine that ends games — 53.5% GIH, 71% play rate. A good maindeck pickup, not a bomb.
Chalk Outline: Synergy build-around. Makes a Detective plus a Clue whenever creatures leave your yard — Numot rates it a strong low-bar payoff, LR B/A in a built graveyard deck but warns the lane is too slow for MKM. 51.9% GIH but +2.0 IWD: a role-player that needs Golgari recursion to pop.
Culvert Ambusher: Solid green disguise beater: a 4/5 for five that forces a creature to block (removing a blocker or eating one), with disguise flexibility. 53.3% GIH is a bit soft but B- and 72% play show it's a reliable body; the block-forcing ETB is real reach in a combat format. Mid-pick Simic/GW.
Fanatical Strength: Solid combat trick. +3/+3 and trample at instant speed is a big blowout that also pushes damage through blockers — a real two-for-one in combat. 56.1% GIH with positive IWD in green aggro/midrange. A reliable role-player; don't over-draft tricks but this one earns a slot.
Flourishing Bloom-Kin: Strong green synergy body. Scales with Forests and disguises into a two-Forest ramp/fixing package, so it's never a dead draw. 58.2% GIH, +2.6 IWD, 90% play — a reliable B-grade playable that's best in mono-green-leaning or ramp shells.
Get a Leg Up: Premium green combat trick — Numot calls it one of the best in the format, capable of +5/+5-or-more blowouts for one mana plus reach for surprise flyer kills. Positive IWD, 68% play rate; a cheap, game-swinging trick that punishes any attack or block.
Glint Weaver: Green curve-topper that stabilizes hard — distributes three counters and gains a wall of life, so if it resolves you're usually winning (Numot). 57.5% GIH with strong drawn numbers confirms it's a mid-game bomblet. A high-value uncommon for grindy green; double copies are deck-defining.
Greenbelt Radical: A premium disguise payoff for green: a 2/2 ward 2 that flips into a 4/4 and pumps your whole board +1/+1 with trample — a one-card team blowout in RG/GW go-wide. 57% GIH, +1.8 IWD, 89% play; take it highly in any green creature deck.
Hard-Hitting Question: Premium green removal — one mana to fight for full power kills almost anything if you have a decent body. Green's best answer, and 57.0% GIH with +2.2 IWD and 88% play rate confirm it. Take it high; the only cost is needing a creature in play.
Hedge Whisperer: Solid utility body. A 1-mana 0/3 that ramps as a blocker early and turns a land into a 5/5 hasty attacker late via collect evidence — a real mana sink with a high floor. 53.4% GIH and 61.6% play rate; a fine green two-slot filler that scales into the late game.
Hide in Plain Sight: Premium green rare: {3}{G} to cloak two of the top five as ward-2 2/2s — "a Collected Company that always hits" (LR), worst case four power for four. 63.2% GIH, +9.6 IWD, 2.0 ALSA — an A-level engine that snowballs disguise/Simic decks. Slam it.
A Killer Among Us: Underrated — LR flipped it to "easily the pick, better than most rares." Five mana for three 1/1 bodies (~6 power spread) plus a deathtouch-and-counters ambush mode is insane when even or ahead. 60.2% GIH, +5.1 IWD, 86% play. Weak purely on defense, but a high pick in go-wide green.
Loxodon Eavesdropper: Solid Simic/value common. A 3/3 for four that investigates on ETB and grows with your second draw each turn — exactly the card-advantage engine GU wants. 56.8% GIH and 85% play; a dependable role-player that snowballs in draw-two decks.
Nervous Gardener: Solid green common and the best early green pick per all three guides — a disguise 2/2 that flips to fetch any basic, giving free fixing that unlocks splashes. 91% play rate, positive IWD. Take it early for the fixing; it gets cut only in fully synergy-locked decks.
Pick Your Poison: Narrow one-mana answer that's mostly a sideboard card — the flying/artifact/enchantment modes miss too often maindeck. 10.3% play and D grade confirm. Board it in vs fliers or key artifacts; don't maindeck.
Pompous Gadabout: Evasive-ish beater with self-protection — a 4/2 for three with hexproof on your turn that can only be blocked by named (nontoken) creatures, so it slips past token boards. 52.6% GIH and 40% play mark it as unremarkable filler; a playable body, not a priority.
The Pride of Hull Clade: Trap-adjacent build-around. A theoretically cheap 2/15 that draws cards off toughness, but you need a fat board to cast it cheaply and it's still just a defender without the pricey activation — 50.5% GIH and 48.4% OH WR say it underperforms its mythic aura. A niche Simic top-end, not a slam.
Rope: Filler equipment. +1/+2 reach and evasion with a sac-to-draw is too slow and clunky for the format; 46.7% GIH and -4.8 IWD confirm the D+. A late-pick clue enabler at best — usually leave it in the board.
Rubblebelt Maverick: Premium green one-drop for graveyard decks: ETB surveil 2 plus a from-yard +1/+1 counter ability that self-exiles (fueling Roots/collect-evidence). 55.6% GIH; Numot flags it as a late-read priority you take over removal in Golgari. A synergy engine, not a slam — grab it in the grave shell.
Sample Collector: Solid green playable. A 2/3 for three that grows your team with +1/+1 counters via collect-evidence is a steady value body, especially in graveyard-fueled GU/BG. 53.4% GIH is fine and B- grade tracks; the counter needs fuel but the floor is a reasonable blocker. Dependable mid-pick.
Sharp-Eyed Rookie: Premium green two-drop. LR grades it A: a 2/2 vigilance for two that grows and investigates whenever a bigger creature enters, generating counters and Clues all game. 59.2% GIH, +5.3 IWD, 91.5% play — first-pickable and miserable to face.
Slime Against Humanity: Trap — LR grades it F, "never does anything useful." Without a stack of Oozes/copies already in exile it's a 2/2 for three, and 44% GIH with a D grade proves the build-around never assembles. Do not play.
They Went This Way: Ramp-plus-Clue fixing that reads better than it plays — 54.4% GIH is fine but the card is slow and low-impact in a format that wants board presence. A role-player for green splash/ramp decks; C-. Fine filler, not a priority.
Topiary Panther: Golgari premium that does everything: a 6/5 trample top-end that also basic-landcycles when flooded, and both feeds the graveyard and grows off Roots. Numot's "every piece of the buffalo" exemplar. 55% GIH with 85% play; the C+ grade underrates it — take it solidly in green.
Tunnel Tipster: Premium green two-drop. Turn-2 ramp into your three-drop, and it snowballs with a counter every time you play a face-down creature — Numot calls it one of the best green commons. 58.8% OH WR is where the value lives; the 90% play rate confirms it. High pick, though LoL notes it's cuttable if you don't need ramp.
Undergrowth Recon: Trap rare. Recurring one land per upkeep does nothing in a two-color aggro-midrange format; LoL flatly calls it a "stinker." 2.5% play rate and null WR — an unplayable healthy-bad rare. Pass every time.
Vengeful Creeper: Clunky overperformer: a {4}{G} 5/5 that disguises and flips to blow up an artifact or enchantment — always has a target in this Clue/equipment format (LoL). 55.8% GIH, positive gd_wr; the built-in disenchant on a big body makes it a reliably good green common. Solid mid-pick.
Vitu-Ghazi Inspector: Solid role-player. A 1/3 reach body for two that, with collect-evidence 6, adds a counter and 2 life — a fine defensive two-drop with graveyard upside. 55.5% GIH, 75% play. The evidence mode is a bonus, not required; a reliable green early play that blocks fliers.
Agrus Kos, Spirit of Justice: Boros bomb. Double strike vigilance on a 2/4 that suspects-then-exiles creatures on ETB and every attack — repeatable removal stapled to an evasive threat. 63.5% GIH, +9.1 IWD, A grade; a slam first pick that ends games alone.
Alquist Proft, Master Sleuth: Bomb — the premier UW signpost. A 3-mana 3/3 vigilance that investigates on ETB and turns into a repeatable X-draw-X-life engine that buries anyone in the mid-game. +5.4 IWD, A grade, ALSA 1.9. First-pick and a reason to be in Azorius.
Anzrag, the Quake-Mole: RG bomb — an 8/4 that either connects for eight or, if blocked, untaps your team and grants an extra combat, plus a lure activation to force it through. 56.3% GIH undersells a card with +5.0 IWD and A-; the ceiling ends games. High pick in Gruul.
Assassin's Trophy: Premium two-mana catch-all removal — destroy ANY permanent for {B}{G}, the basic-land downside irrelevant in Limited. B+ grade, and the 48.3% OH vs 54.4% GD split shows it's a late-game answer, not an early play, which drags raw GIH to 52.1%. First-pickable in any BG deck.
Aurelia, the Law Above: Format-defining bomb — LSV's personal favorite. A 4/4 flying vigilance haste for five is already premium, and in any wide Boros deck the card draw and 3-damage/3-life triggers take over — 60.3% GIH, 91% play rate, 1.4 ALSA. First-pick, splash-worthy.
Blood Spatter Analysis: Premium Rakdos removal + engine. A 2-mana enchantment that Shocks on ETB, then mills and eventually reanimates a creature as the board trades — 56.5% GIH and +4.3 IWD reward BR aggro's constant deaths. A great early BR pick that snowballs a grind.
Buried in the Garden: The reason to be Selesnya (LR calls it A-): {2}{G}{W} O-Ring on a nonland permanent that ALSO ramps you a mana of any color off the enchanted land. 59.7% GIH, +5.3 IWD — removal plus fixing plus ramp in one card. Premium GW pickup, take highly.
Coerced to Kill: Premium removal — the best kind of aura here. It steals their creature AND shrinks it to a 1/1 deathtouch, so you get their body as a repeatable deathtouch blocker/attacker. 58.8% GIH, +6.4 IWD, B+ grade. Effectively a two-for-one removal spell for UB; prioritize it.
Crowd-Control Warden: Good GW payoff. A 4/4-plus that enters scaling with your board width and disguises to flip up as a blowout later, dodging sorcery removal. 54.6% GIH and 73% play mark a dependable curve-topper for go-wide Selesnya; solid, not splashy.
Curious Cadaver: Middling UB gold uncommon. A 3/1 flyer that recurs itself when you sac a Clue is nice recursion in the Clue-heavy Dinner Party deck, but the fragile body and 50% GIH (with a weak 47% OH WR) make it a role-player, not a driver. Fine synergy inclusion.
Deadly Complication: Efficient BR removal — unconditional destroy for three mana, with a suspect-synergy rider as upside. 54.6% GIH and +2.5 IWD make it a reliable playable; the flexible mode helps in suspect decks. Solid removal, prioritize in Rakdos.
Detective's Satchel: Powerful grindy value engine — two Clues on ETB plus a Thopter factory once you're saccing artifacts, doubly good in Rakdos/Izzet splashes with Clue payoffs. 58.3% GIH and +5.2 IWD on 70% play confirm the engine overdelivers; take it high in UR/artifact-value decks.
Dog Walker: One of the best commons in the format — '11th-pick Dog Walker is busted.' A 3/1 vigilance whose disguise flip makes two 2/2 Dogs, and the X/1 body dodges the format's lack of 1-toughness removal. Early 'bad on defense' reads are superseded; 57.8% GIH, 91% play rate. Best in Boros go-wide, never cut from GW.
Doppelgang: Bomb finisher for Simic. Scales from a clone at five to a game-over play at eight-plus; 62.4% GIH, a massive +9.3 IWD and 64.7% GD WR make it one of the best late-game closers in the set despite the modest C+ grade. LSV's favorite — first-pick in UG.
Drag the Canal: Solid UB instant that makes a 2/2 detective and, if a creature died, adds life, surveil 2 and a Clue — easy to turn on in a grindy Dimir deck. 55.3% GIH with a strong +4.6 IWD; B+ and instant-speed value make it a reliable go-to spell. High Dimir pick.
Etrata, Deadly Fugitive: Strong build-around bomb for UB disguise/assassin. A 1/4 deathtoucher that discounts your face-down flips and mills-plus-cloaks off Assassin damage — a real engine that also blocks all day. 58.4% GIH, +7.7 IWD, ALSA 2.1. High pick in Dimir; the deathtouch body alone is playable.
Evidence Examiner: Strong Simic engine. A two-mana 2/2 that turns your graveyard into a stream of Clues via repeatable collect-evidence — steady card advantage in GU value. +4.2 IWD and 71% play confirm the engine hums; a high pick in Simic/Golgari grind decks.
Ezrim, Agency Chief: Set-defining bomb — the standout numbers say it all: 63% GIH, a monstrous +10.9 IWD, A+ grade. A 5/5 flyer that investigates twice and sacrifices artifacts to gain hexproof/lifelink/vigilance is near-impossible to beat once it lands. Slam over almost anything in UW.
Faerie Snoop: Reality undercut the hype: a flexible 1/4 flyer with disguise card selection, but mana-hungry with diminishing returns and weak in tempo Detectives. 54.0% GIH is fine, not premium. A good UB role-player — take one or two, don't overload; the 'too many Snoops' problem is real.
Gadget Technician: The top hybrid gold common — hardcast a 3/2 that makes a flying Thopter on four, or disguise for {3} and flip cheaply off double-hybrid mana, and it flexes into UR/RG/RW. 55.8% GIH and 77% play; Kenji's favorite common disguise creature. Reliable mid-to-high pick.
Gleaming Geardrake: Strong UR-artifacts enabler — 'happy first-pick.' A flier that Investigates on entry and grows off every artifact sacrifice, and the free Clue means it always trades up. 60.3% GIH and +6.7 IWD are premium-uncommon numbers; the signpost for UR artifacts.
Granite Witness: Solid WU workhorse. A 3/2 flyer with vigilance (or 2/2 disguise that draws-adjacent taps on flip) that wheels often — both experts note wheeling means the WU lane is open. 55.9% GIH; a reliable, better-than-filler common that anchors Azorius.
Ill-Timed Explosion: The best wrath in the set used right (LR): {2}{U}{R} draws two, then optionally discards two to deal X damage to each creature (X = biggest MV discarded). 60.5% GIH, +8.1 IWD, A grade — a flexible sweeper-or-Divination that's "always good versus white" (Numot). Premium Izzet bomb.
Insidious Roots: Build-around payoff for BG graveyard — headliner but demanding. It makes escalating Plant tokens whenever creature cards leave your yard and ramps off tokens. The split stats (51.6% GIH but +2.4 IWD, sub-49% opening-hand) show it's a synergy card that needs the deck. Only pick it committed to Golgari recursion.
Izoni, Center of the Web: Top-tier BG bomb. +14.5 IWD and 65.3% GIH — the best numbers on the sheet: a 5/4 menace that spits out Spider tokens off collect-evidence and cashes them for cards and life. A grade, 92% play; a slam-dunk Golgari engine that grinds any game away.
Judith, Carnage Connoisseur: Overrated BR rare — LR's "biggest underperformer" at 50% GIH. The spell payoff plus black both failed her, and the 3/4 body doesn't carry a durdly plan. Numot calls her "just okay." A playable in a spells-dense Rakdos deck, but nowhere near her B+ grade; don't first-pick.
Kaya, Spirits' Justice: WB bomb planeswalker — 60.1% GIH, a massive +9.4 IWD, and a -2 that's a two-sided removal spell while the +1 defends her and the passive snowballs. A- undersells it; this is a first-pick that anchors Orzhov. Take over almost anything.
Kellan, Inquisitive Prodigy: A premium Simic rare and near-bomb: MDFC that ramps/investigates early or comes down as a 3/4 flying vigilance that draws when it attacks and kills an artifact. 60.6% GIH, +7.5 IWD, 63% OH, 84% play — flexibility plus evasion plus card advantage. Take it very early in UG.
Kylox, Visionary Inventor: Trap. A 7-mana build-around with conflicting requirements — you need creatures to sac AND spells in your library — that 'really missed.' 44.4% GIH and 5.6% play rate are damning. Leave this rare in the box.
Kylox's Voltstrider: Strong UR value engine. A 4/4 vehicle for three that recasts your exiled instants/sorceries on attack, generating repeated spell value; 56% GIH and +4.1 IWD back the B+. Crew 2 is easy in Izzet; a high-priority UR mythic that snowballs.
Lazav, Wearer of Faces: Strong UB rare: a 2/3 for two that Investigates on attack and can flip Clues into copies of exiled creatures — grindy card advantage plus a scaling threat. 57.6% GIH with +7.3 IWD confirms it takes over long games. B+; a high Dimir pick that rewards a graveyard-heavy build.
Leyline of the Guildpact: Trap — Numot: "more a fun card than a good card." In a two-color deck it just fixes mana you already have and does nothing else; the free-turn-zero clause is a novelty. 43.8% GIH, F grade, 14% play. Not a real Limited card.
Lightning Helix: Premium Boros removal. Instant 3-to-anything plus 3 life is exactly what RW wants — reach, tempo, and a swing against aggro; both guides call it disgusting but color-committing. 58.9% GIH, B grade; a high pick that pushes you firmly into Boros.
Meddling Youths: Fine Boros signpost, not a bomb. A 4/5 haste for five with a hard-to-trigger investigate (attack with three-plus) has an awkward stat line and cost per Numot. 54% GIH but negative IWD — a solid RW body that signals the archetype without being why Boros is good.
Niv-Mizzet, Guildpact: A five-color trap outside a dedicated fixing deck — 56.2% GIH looks fine but the 53.5% OH and 43% play rate show it's clunky to cast and dead in hand early. When it connects it takes over, but the WUBRG cost fights the two-color format. Only for heavy-fixing pods; C+ is generous.
No More Lies: The best counter in the format but still a situational reactive card — {W}{U} Mana Leak that exiles, strong against bombs and disguise flips. 55.7% GIH and 57% OH are good, but 46% play shows many decks don't want a hold-up counter. Solid WU playable; prioritize below proactive cards.
Officious Interrogation: Underwhelming rare — mostly a fringe Azorius Clue engine. It only pays off with a big board on both sides and does nothing to affect it; 49.0% GIH with a bad -3.2 IWD and 46% OH WR show it's a win-more that clutters your hand early. The B grade is a trap; playable only in dedicated Clue/artifact WU.
Private Eye: Premium WU uncommon — the top one. A 3/3 Detective lord that makes a Detective unblockable when you draw your second card; 58.7% GIH and +4.6 IWD deliver on the anthem/tempo. Numot: two copies is game-winning. Prioritize in detectives.
Rakdos, Patron of Chaos: Bomb, full stop (LR: A+). A {4}{B}{R} 6/6 flying trample that each end step makes them sac two permanents OR draws you two — you win either way. 60.7% GIH, +9.6 IWD, 1.4 ALSA. First-pick and splash-worthy; the ceiling of any BR deck.
Rakish Scoundrel: Filler. A 3/3 deathtouch for four with an indestructible-granting ETB/flip is a fine body plus a combat/removal-protection trick, but ALSA 6.7 and 29% play rate mark it a niche BG disguise card. 51.8% GIH is replacement-level. Playable if you're in Golgari, otherwise a late body.
Relive the Past: Trap for maindecks. The B+ grade collides with a 47.9% GIH and -2.4 IWD: a seven-mana reanimation that needs specific artifact/land/enchantment fuel in the yard and does nothing to stabilize an empty board. Niche GW ramp payoff only; the live data says pass.
Repulsive Mutation: Premium GU/GW gold uncommon and one of the best — a pump-plus-counter two-for-one that grows your board while taxing their spell. Excellent +5.8 IWD, 60% GIH, 71% play rate. A high pick in Simic/Selesnya; flexible tempo and card advantage in one instant.
Riftburst Hellion: Vanilla-ish disguise beater — a 6/7 reach for seven, or a 2/2 ward-2 on turn three that flips later. 53.6% GIH is exactly average; the disguise flexibility keeps it from being dead but it does nothing tricky. A fine RG curve-filler, not a priority.
Rune-Brand Juggler: Aggressive Rakdos two-drop with a removal mode — a 2/2 that suspects a creature (menace + a loot-adjacent aggro enabler) and can later sac a suspected creature to shrink a blocker -5/-5. Numot likes it as aggressive filler; 54.9% GIH and +2.1 IWD confirm a fine early play in RB.
Sanguine Savior: Solid WB/Boros hybrid common. A 2/1 flying lifelink is a fine evasive body and disguise gives it flexibility plus a lifelink-granting flip to steal races — 54.1% GIH, 68% play rate. A good role-player closer, not a bomb; passable in a pinch per the late read.
Shady Informant: Filler BR body. A 4/2 that Shocks on death, optionally coming down as a disguise creature — fine incidental value but 51.8% GIH and a 34.8% play rate mark it as a replaceable curve-filler. Playable in dedicated BR, otherwise a bench card.
Soul Search: Weak targeted discard: {W}{B} to exile a nonland card (with a token if it's cheap), but sorcery-speed hand attack is low-impact in a creature-combat format. D+, 14.7% play, negative IWD — a sideboard card against specific bombs, not a maindeck pick.
Sumala Sentry: Solid Selesnya (WG) disguise payoff. A 1/3 reach two-drop that grows itself and your flipping creatures with double counters — real value in a disguise/face-down deck. 56.8% GIH, 58% opening-hand WR, B grade. The floor is a fine blocker; the ceiling in WG is strong. Good early pick in that pair.
Teysa, Opulent Oligarch: WB bomb engine. +10.0 IWD, A- grade — a deathtouch 2/3 that manufactures Clues off any opponent losing life and converts each into a flying Spirit, snowballing inexorably. LR's inevitability groan-test; a premium Orzhov pick that wins the long game.
Tin Street Gossip: Solid Gruul signpost — a 4/4 vigilance for four that also fixes RG mana for disguise/flip costs. Enables the archetype's flip-heavy plan without being a dead do-nothing. 54% GIH; a fine curve piece that pulls double duty in Gruul.
Tolsimir, Midnight's Light: Format bomb — the set's best gold card by the numbers: 63.5% GIH, a staggering +10.2 IWD, A grade (LR says A+). Five mana for a lifelink body plus a 5/5 trample Wolf that forces blocks — nearly impossible to survive. First-pick Selesnya, wheels almost never.
Treacherous Greed: A big Orzhov payoff that needs a board — sac an attacker to draw three and swing the life total six, huge when it connects but dead without a creature that dealt damage. 52.8% GIH and 39% play show the setup cost bites; a strong reward card in aggressive WB, cuttable in slower builds.
Trostani, Three Whispers: Selesnya bomb. A 3-mana 4/4 that can hand out deathtouch, vigilance, or double strike makes it nearly unkillable in combat and turns any creature into a threat — 60.5% GIH, +7.5 IWD, 1.6 ALSA. First-pick caliber in GW.
Urgent Necropsy: Premium flexible removal. A modal instant that can blow up an artifact, creature, enchantment and planeswalker at once; the collect-evidence cost is real but the huge +7.8 IWD and 61.8% GD WR (well above 54.9% OH — it's a card you want to draw into a board) confirm it overperforms its B-. Take it in BG.
Vannifar, Evolved Enigma: Format-defining mythic: a 3/4 for four that each combat free-cloaks from hand (a 2/2 threat plus a hidden card) or pumps colorless creatures. 61.2% GIH, +9.6 IWD, near-universal play — "just way too good" (Numot), "completely absurd" (LR). A bomb that locks you into Simic; slam it.
Warleader's Call: Bomb — the Boros (WR) signpost payoff. A team-wide anthem that also pings each opponent for 1 on every creature ETB closes games fast in a go-wide deck. 59.8% GIH, +4.7 IWD, ALSA 1.8, A grade. Nearly unbeatable if you're the aggressor; take it very high.
Wispdrinker Vampire: Strong WB payoff. A 2/4 flyer that drains and gains each time a power-2-or-less creature enters, with a lifelink/deathtouch overrun as a mana sink — the pint-size engine Orzhov wants. 55.6% GIH and B grade; a high pick in go-wide WB.
Worldsoul's Rage: Solid RG splash finisher and mana-sink X-removal-plus-ramp — note the huge OH/GD split (48% opening vs 56% drawn), so it's dead early but a game-ender in the late game. LoL frames it as the red splash payoff for BG. A strong top-end where you can afford the X.
Yarus, Roar of the Old Gods: RG disguise engine and a strong standalone 4/4 that hastes your team — 57.0% GIH, +4.7 IWD, and LSV rates it P1P1-worthy. Even without a face-down build it's a fine body; with disguise fodder it draws cards and recurs. High pick in Gruul; B+/A- range.
Cease // Desist: Flexible splashable answer, mostly for the Cease half: cheap {1}{B/G} graveyard hate that cantrips and gains life, with Desist as a rare artifact/enchantment sweeper. 54.2% GIH on only 27% play means it's a good card few decks stretch for; a fine role-player when the mana lines up.
Flotsam // Jetsam: Fringe graveyard/mill card. Front half is a cheap mill-plus-Clue cantrip, back half a pricey steal-their-graveyard payoff that rarely lines up — 50.4% GIH with negative IWD and a poor 46.7% OH WR. A niche Sultai self-mill pickup, filler at best.
Fuss // Bother: Premium Azorius go-wide payoff. Bother makes three flyers and surveils; Fuss pumps your whole team as a finisher — exactly what WU tokens/flyers wants. 58.7% GIH and +2.1 IWD across an 87.9% play rate. A high pick in the format's best-supported archetype.
Hustle // Bustle: Weak split card — Numot flatly "doesn't like it." The Hustle half is a marginal falter, and the Bustle overrun costs {4}{R/G}{R/G} and needs a board to matter. 51.7% GIH, negative IWD, 39% play. A fringe go-wide finisher; mostly a sideboard/filler slot.
Push // Pull: Premium removal — a top early uncommon. Push is efficient tempo removal (destroy a tapped creature) and Pull is a game-ending reanimation swing; the hybrid cost lets nearly any deck cast Push. 55.3% GIH, ALSA 3.1, 86% play. Value dips only if you can't cast both halves. Prioritize.
Cryptex: Trap rare. LR's F is right: a two-mana rock that demands ~15 collect-evidence activations before the surveil-3-draw-3 payoff unlocks — it doesn't do the thing in a normal game. The 51.2% GIH is fixing/inclusion noise; skip.
Gravestone Strider: Underrated colorless role-player — Numot's "all-star" in graveyard decks. A 1/3 that fixes any color and self-exiles for graveyard hate/Roots synergy earns its 65% play rate as early fixing plus late utility. Fine glue in artifact/graveyard builds; filler elsewhere.
Lumbering Laundry: Overpriced colorless filler — a 4/5 for five with a near-useless scry-face-down ability, playable as a disguise 2/2 but that's it. 51.2% GIH, -3.1 IWD, and 9.9% play mark it as replacement-level. Only if you're short bodies; C-.
Magnetic Snuffler: Below-replacement colorless top-end — a 4/4 for five that only pays off if you have an Equipment in the yard to reanimate, otherwise a vanilla body. 48.7% GIH, 45.7% OH, 12% play, D grade confirm it whiffs too often. Skip outside a dedicated equipment deck.
Magnifying Glass: Filler mana rock — a slow ramp/Clue artifact that's too weak for this format. 46.8% GIH, a brutal -4.4 IWD, and 9% play rate all say it costs you tempo for little. Skip unless you specifically need artifact-count for synergy.
Sanitation Automaton: Solid glue two-drop. A 2/1 with surveil 1 that slots into any deck and fills MKM's shortage of good two-drops; LoL's "Golden Egg co-winner" with a high floor. 54.2% GIH and 72% play rate — a reliable, colorless curve-filler you're happy to run.
